newsitem.title: USA: Quick/Reilly seen drawing wide range of bids.
newsitem.headline: Quick/Reilly seen drawing wide range of bids.

text.p: Discount broker Quick & Reilly Group Inc is likely to find a buyer and could draw bids from the mid- to upper-$30 per share range.

Analysts and arbitrageurs said Tuesday the company would be an attractive addition for a bank or other financial institution, although it does not possess the premium businesses like investment banking and underwriting currently sought as entrees into the securities business.
As such, the company may not command more than $33 or $34 per share, they said.

However, they noted Quick's less flashy operations, like securities clearing, could provide predictable and even cash flow to sustain a broader move into equities by the right buyer -- augmented by Quick's client list -- and justify a higher price.
Earlier, published reports said Quick had retained Goldman Sach and Gleacher NatWest to help it mull a possible transaction. Quick declined to detail any possible deal.
Goldman declined to comment and Gleacher did not return calls seeking comment.
Quick shares rose to an all-time high 32-3/4 on the news in unusually heavy trade, then settled back to 31-11/16, a gain of 2-6/16, or 8.1 percent.

"The company has a book value of $11 (per share) on my machine and it will go for three times book," said an arb who argued a takeover premium would not be that significant because Quick basically provides "commodity-type" services within the equity market.

Added a second arb: "It is a big discount broker and client operation. It is not an innovator. But if you are a bank you might want a certain amount of transaction volume and (sales) reps to pump products."
One published report suggested First Union Corp and Barnett Banks Inc as potential bidders. Both companies declined to comment.

Quick & Reilly's primary businesses are the discount brokerage, U.S. Clearing Corp, which provides stock clearing and execution services for brokers and banks, JCC Specialists, an NYSE specialist firm, and Nash Weiss & Co, a market maker in Nasdaq-listed shares.

Arguing a fuller valuation, Perrin Long, an independent analyst covering the securities business, said the company could go for somewhere around $40 to $45 per share, a premium of about 33 to 35 percent. Quick & Reilly is an extremely profitable operation."

"It makes a great deal of sense for Quick & Reilly to be sold. Their timing is almost perfect. We are at the top of the longest bull market in history and they would be selling at the top -- one of the great goals in life," said Sheldon Grodsky of Grodsky Associates Inc.
Quick family members are among the company's top executives and the family controls about 40 percent of the company's stock.

Based on 38.55 million shares outstanding, a $33 per share deal would be worth about $1.27 billion, while a $45 bid would be worth about $1.73 billion, both excluding any debt assumption or other contingencies.
